title: CONTROL Resonant walkthrough
description: Understand how Dylan's Journey, Jesse Quests, World Quests, Faults and Zone activities differ, then follow the route that matches the objective in front of you.
imageAlt: Trains suspended along impossible directions in an official CONTROL Resonant screenshot
introTitle: Identify the objective before choosing a route
intro: The full game mixes campaign priorities, optional stories, traversal rewards and short Zone activities. This hub explains those layers and links only to routes whose steps can be supported without inventing a complete mission order.

cards.title: Dylan's Journey
cards.text: The campaign lets Dylan prioritize more than one active lead. Follow the objective that advances the system or Zone you need instead of assuming every visible marker is mandatory.

cards.title: World Quests
cards.text: Optional stories give Manhattan's inhabitants and strange events their own context. They should not be confused with every collectible or combat activity on the map.

cards.title: Jesse Quests
cards.text: These optional quests award traversal powers such as the double jump and air dash described in full-game coverage, making them especially useful before returning to blocked routes.

cards.title: Faults
cards.text: IGN presents Metro Fault as one of the dungeon-like Faults, associated with a traversal reward. The preview is indexed separately from a retail step-by-step completion.

sections.title: How to use a route without losing the main objective
paragraphs: Read the activity name, Zone and reward type before following a route. Full-game coverage confirms that side missions can unlock movement or build options, while short arcade-style challenges are better treated as practice and progression than campaign chapters.
bullets: Use named landmarks instead of invented map coordinates.
Separate required progression from optional exploration.
Check the demonstrated loadout before copying a combat approach.
Keep boss advice and reward verification attached to the actual encounter.

note: The game is available to reviewers, but this site has not independently reproduced a complete campaign route. Exact triggers, coordinates and missable conditions remain excluded until they can be checked directly.

title: CONTROL Resonant Bosses — Read the Fight Before You Commit
description: Meet the Central Resonant, see the arena hazards shown in its fight, and learn how Resonant victories affect Dylan's Combat Ability choices.
imageAlt: Dylan facing a fiery Resonant in official CONTROL Resonant promotional media
intro: Resonants are optional major encounters as well as sources of Combat Ability choices. Full-game coverage supports a prepare, attempt, explore and return approach; this page does not pretend every shown entity already has a verified name or drop table.

sections.title: Do you have to defeat every Resonant?
paragraphs: Not every Resonant is mandatory. Remedy's lead level designer says players are not forced to defeat every encounter or one particular boss. The story may require a number of victories from a larger set, but the required count and full roster have not been published.

That makes boss choice part of route planning. It does not tell you which encounter is easiest, which power a named boss grants, or whether a particular fight can be skipped in the final game without consequences.

cards.title: Combat Ability rewards
cards.text: Resonant victories connect boss progression to the build system. Some rewards involve choices; a general rule is not enough to name an individual boss's exact ability.

cards.title: A changing world
cards.text: The August developer interview describes harder encounters as Resonants fall. A defeated boss affects more than the immediate arena.

cards.title: New Game Plus
cards.text: Later runs broaden the combinations available from boss abilities. Compare the confirmed carryover rules before planning a second run.

sections.title: Prepare for the arena, the Falter window and the next attempt
paragraphs: A useful strategy needs to state the game version, loadout, settings, telegraphs and reward evidence. Reviews consistently recommend leaving an optional Resonant, improving the build and returning when a fight becomes a damage or survival wall.
bullets: Learn what changes the safe area of the arena.
Distinguish a ranged attack from a persistent ground hazard.
Use Falter and executions to create health-recovery windows instead of trading indefinitely.
Test one setup change at a time.
Treat phase counts, timings and damage values as unverified until reproduced.

note: Only named encounters shown so far appear here. Exact phases, weaknesses and rewards need to be checked in the released game.

title: CONTROL Resonant builds & progression
description: Understand how Aberrant Forms, Combat Abilities, Talents and Artifacts fit together. Plan your setup with sourced mechanics rather than untested damage rankings.
imageAlt: Dylan wielding a large Aberrant weapon against fungal enemies
intro: Start with the melee-to-Power loop, then diagnose the actual failure: closing distance, breaking Falter, recovering health, controlling a crowd or surviving a boss phase. Change the layer that answers that problem.

table.caption: The four connected build systems
rows: Dodge Attack visible in the preview
Three slots initially; four in NG+

steps.title: Melee restores ability power
steps.text: Close-range attacks help supply the resource used by Combat Abilities.

steps.title: Abilities create openings
steps.text: Abilities can interrupt enemies, expose Falter windows and control threats the current Form cannot safely reach.

steps.title: Executions restore the fight
steps.text: Breaking Falter enables an execution that restores health and grants a temporary melee boost; Dominance can turn a vulnerable enemy into a temporary ally.

sections.title: Plan a loadout around an actual problem

cards.title: Reach and crowd pressure
cards.text: Compare the role of your Primary and Secondary Forms. The goal is to solve your encounter problem, not equip a name that sounds strongest.

cards.title: Conditions and tradeoffs
cards.text: Read when an Artifact activates and what it gives up. A passive that never triggers in your playstyle is not a useful headline bonus.

cards.title: Talent and respec decisions
cards.text: Use the zone XP and Talent guide to understand progression. Respec All is visible in preview UI; final refund and cost rules remain distinct questions.

sections.title: First playthrough versus New Game Plus
paragraphs: Remedy's NG+ description adds further Talent nodes, a fourth Artifact slot and broader Combat Ability combinations. Story-gated traversal unlocks are an exception to carryover. A first-run setup and an NG+ setup therefore need different assumptions.
bullets: Check the available slot count before copying an Artifact combination.
Distinguish Combat Abilities from traversal skills.
Account for harder encounters rather than comparing damage alone.

note: There is no tested best-build tier list here yet. No DPS figures, boss clear times or final numerical rankings are invented.
